summary: Two angels reach Lot’s home in Sodom, where a crowd demands sexual access to the visitors and Lot shockingly offers his daughters; the angels intervene and lead Lot’s family out. Fire destroys the cities and plain, Lot’s wife becomes a pillar of salt after looking back, and in a cave Lot’s daughters intoxicate him to conceive Moab and Ben Ammi.
whyItMatters: The chapter includes attempted sexual violence, a father’s offer to expose daughters, mass destruction, and intoxicated incest. Its rescue narrative must be read with those harms in full view rather than using the episode as a simple moral label for an entire city.

context.author: Genesis names no historical writer. Jewish and Christian tradition associates the Torah with Moses; the book briefing describes older traditions shaped into a final literary form, without a settled account of every stage.
context.audience: The book addresses Israel through a story of shared human origins and the family from whom Israel traces its ancestry; no single first audience is named in this chapter.
context.date: The narrated events belong to primeval or ancestral time, not to a securely dated writing event. Major stages of Genesis are often placed across the monarchic to Persian periods, with exact models and dates debated.
context.setting: Lot’s house in Sodom, the route to Zoar, the destroyed plain, and a mountain cave.
context.literaryForm: Threat-and-escape narrative followed by destruction notice and an origin story for Moab and Ammon.

before.text: Abraham has asked whether righteous residents should die with a wicked city, and Yahweh agreed to spare Sodom if ten are found. The two visitors now arrive there.

here.text: Distinguish the crowd’s threat, Lot’s offer of his daughters, the angels’ rescue, the city’s destruction, and the troubling cave aftermath.

after.text: Abraham next travels to Gerar, where he again calls Sarah his sister and a ruler takes her into his household.

outline.heading: Visitors sheltered; crowd gathers
outline.note: Lot welcomes the visitors, and men of Sodom demand sexual access to them.

outline.heading: Lot’s offer and angelic intervention
outline.note: Lot offers his daughters, the crowd threatens him, and the visitors pull him inside.

outline.heading: Warning and reluctant escape
outline.note: The angels warn relatives and lead the lingering household out toward Zoar.

outline.heading: Destruction and Lot’s wife
outline.note: Fire destroys the plain, Lot’s wife becomes salt, and Abraham sees the smoke.

outline.heading: Cave, intoxication, and children
outline.note: Lot’s daughters make him drunk and conceive the ancestors of Moab and Ammon.

keyVerses.text: See now, I have two virgin daughters. Please let me bring them out to you, and you may do to them what seems good to you. Only don’t do anything to these men, because they have come under the shadow of my roof.”
keyVerses.why: Lot offers his daughters to the crowd, exposing them to threatened sexual violence.

keyVerses.text: But he lingered; and the men grabbed his hand, his wife’s hand, and his two daughters’ hands, Yahweh being merciful to him; and they took him out, and set him outside of the city.
keyVerses.why: The rescue occurs while Lot lingers, and the narrative attributes the intervention to mercy.

keyVerses.text: They made their father drink wine that night: and the firstborn went in, and lay with her father. He didn’t know when she lay down, nor when she arose.
keyVerses.why: The first cave episode explicitly says Lot is drunk and unaware of what happens.

questions.question: What does the crowd demand from the visitors?
questions.answer: Men from across Sodom surround the house and demand that Lot bring out the visitors for sex. Lot calls the act wicked; the scene depicts a threatened assault, not a consensual relationship.

questions.question: Does Lot protect everyone in his household?
questions.answer: No. He offers his virgin daughters to the crowd in place of the visitors and tells the men to do to them what seems good. The angels later pull him inside, but the text does not endorse his offer as care for the daughters.

questions.question: What is Zoar in the escape?
questions.answer: It is the small nearby city Lot asks to reach rather than fleeing to the mountains. His request is granted, and its name is linked here with its smallness.

questions.question: Why do the angels pull Lot’s family out by hand?
questions.answer: They urge departure at dawn, but Lot lingers. The narrative says Yahweh is merciful and has the visitors take him, his wife, and the two daughters outside before the destruction.

questions.question: Does the chapter describe loss beyond the people threatening the visitors?
questions.answer: Yes. It says the cities, the plain, all their inhabitants, and what grew on the ground are overthrown. That broad destruction is morally difficult and should not be narrated as though only the attackers at Lot’s door died.

questions.question: What is said about Lot’s wife?
questions.answer: She looks back after the escape warning and becomes a pillar of salt. The chapter gives her no speech or inner motive, so it does not establish why she looked or justify additional blame beyond its stated sequence.

questions.question: Can the cave pregnancies be called consensual intercourse by Lot?
questions.answer: The daughters deliberately make him drink wine on two nights, and the account twice says he does not know when they lie down or rise. It portrays impaired awareness and incest; the daughters state fear for the family line, but that motive does not make the act consensual.

questions.question: Who are Moab and Ben Ammi here?
questions.answer: They are the sons born to Lot’s daughters after the cave incidents, named as ancestors of the Moabites and children of Ammon. The genealogy is part of the story’s account of neighboring peoples, not a statement about their modern descendants.

glossary.def: The small city Lot is allowed to reach before destruction falls on the plain.
The form Lot’s wife becomes after looking back during the escape.
The bread Lot bakes for his visitors before the crowd surrounds his house.
